users.$comment_index: Required for LeaderboardRepository's orderByChild('wins') query to work efficiently at scale — without this, Firebase logs a warning and falls back to an unindexed scan.

$uid.$comment: No blanket '.write' at this level, deliberately: RTDB rules cascade permissively downward, so a parent '.write: true' would grant write access to EVERY child including coins/wins/xp/level, no matter what those children's own rules say. Only the specific cosmetic fields below get a '.write' rule at all; coins/level/xp/wins/gamesPlayed/lastDailyRewardClaimed*/ownedItems have none, so they fall through to root's default '.write: false' and are reachable only by Cloud Functions (initializeUserProfile, claimDailyReward, purchaseItem, and the stats update inside submitMove) running with the Admin SDK.

$roomId.$comment: Private rooms are protected by their unguessable code (e.g. ATHAR4587), not by pre-join membership — a joiner must be able to read a room's metadata (status/maxPlayers/players) BEFORE their own player node exists, to decide whether joining is even possible (room full? already started?). Any authenticated user who has the code can read the room; nobody can read the *list* of all rooms (no rules exist for rooms with a wildcard read at the top level), so codes can't be enumerated.

$playerId.$comment: The room-full/already-started checks in FirebaseRoomRepository.joinRoom() run inside a client transaction, which a malicious client could skip by writing straight to this path — so the same capacity check is re-enforced here at the rules layer using root.child() lookups, independent of the app's own code.

gameState.$comment: PHASE 6: gameState is now Cloud-Function-only. The six callable functions in functions/src/index.ts (startGame, rollDice, submitMove, forceSkipExpiredTurn, leaveGame, requestRematch) use the Admin SDK, which bypasses these rules entirely — that is the actual mechanism that makes this server-authoritative rather than merely client-side-validated-and-hoped-for. A modified client APK can no longer write a fabricated gameState directly to Realtime Database; every write to this path MUST go through one of those functions, each of which re-derives the legal move/turn/timer state from LudoGameEngine (the TypeScript port in functions/src/ludoEngine.ts, kept in lockstep with the Kotlin client engine) before writing anything.

chat.$comment: Basic spam protection per section 13: messages are immutable once created (no edits/deletes, so no way to spam-edit a single message into new content), capped at 200 chars, and 'sentAt' must equal the server's own request time (RTDB's special 'now' variable) rather than a client-supplied value — this stops a modified client from backdating messages to make them look like they arrived faster than physically possible. A minimum-interval-between-sends throttle is enforced client-side (ChatViewModel); a fully server-side rate limit would need a Cloud Function tracking each sender's last message time, which is a reasonable Phase 9+ hardening step if chat abuse becomes a real problem.

$messageId..write: auth != null && !data.exists() && newData.child('senderId').val() === auth.uid && root.child('rooms/' + $roomId + '/players/' + auth.uid).exists()
